chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from al-Husayn ibn Abdillah, who said:

Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and Ibn Abi Ya'fur traveled together. One of them ate from the slaughtered meat of the Jew and the Christian, while the other refused to eat it. They met at the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him. He asked, 'Which of you refused?' He said, 'I.' He said, 'You did well.'

key_terms.أَحْسَنْتَ: You did well / You are correct

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of Jews and Christians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a nuanced juristic debate between two prominent companions, Al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and Ibn Abi Ya'fur, regarding the permissibility of consuming meat slaughtered by the People of the Book. Imam al-Sadiq’s affirmation of the one who refused suggests that while such meat is technically permissible (*halal*), exercising caution (*ihtiyat*) or preferring to avoid it is a praiseworthy act, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on both textual permissibility and spiritual prudence. This incident underscores the dynamic nature of *fiqh* where individual discretion and context play significant roles in applying general rulings.
